label: start of copy phase (DEL step and first two recalls) in long sequences
explanation: Fires almost only at the start of the copy phase: the <DEL> step (40% of mass) and the next two steps that output orig(1) and orig(2) (55%). Rate grows strongly with L; L=8-9 holds 84% of mass and L<=5 almost none. It is essentially silent during the original-input phase (3% of mass, mostly at the last input positions of L=9) and in the late copy phase. Even in these positions it fires only about 5% of the time. Which token is being output modulates it somewhat (z, l, k, 3, h favored; out-token lift up to ~5.6x), but no token rule gives clean precision: adding an out-token set lifts dev precision only to 0.21 and cuts recall to 0.49. The predicate covers about 79% of activation mass on dev, with precision around 0.10. Higher activations are covered slightly better (quartile coverage 0.69 to 0.81). No sharper magnitude modulator was found.
